problems.problem: (a) Factorize the expression: $$(a+b)^2(b+c)^2(c+a)^2+abc\{2(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)+abc\}$$ (b) Find the sum of the series $$\frac{1}{1\cdot2\cdot3}+\frac{1}{2\cdot3\cdot4}+\frac{1}{3\cdot4\cdot5}+\frac{1}{4\cdot5\cdot6}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n\cdot(n+1)\cdot(n+2)}$$ up to $n$ terms and verify the result using the method of induction.
Find the domain and range of the given function $f(x)=\dfrac{1+x^2}{1-x^2}$.

An oil cylinder having base radius $2$ m and height $2$ m is lying parallel to the ground. If the level of oil is at a height of $1.5$ m from the lower surface of the cylinder, how much oil is there in the cylinder?

A funnel-shaped chimney is built using a partial right circular cone (removing the part containing the vertex) and a right circular cylinder, the measurements of which are as follows: the radii of the parallel circular bases of the partial cone are $10$ m and $3$ m; the base radius and height of the cylinder are $3$ m and $10$ m respectively. How much area of iron sheet is required to build this chimney? What is the volume of the chimney?

A hollow sphere is placed inside a cube of side length $a$ so that the sphere touches every face of the cube. What is the maximum height of the right circular cylinder of base radius half that of the sphere which can be accommodated inside the sphere? Find the ratio of the volume of the open space between the cube and the sphere to that between the sphere and the cylinder.

A point on a diagonal of a rectangular parallelepiped of dimensions $1.5\text{ m}\times1.2\text{ m}\times0.9\text{ m}$ is taken so that the point divides the diagonal in the ratio $1:3$. A sphere of radius $0.1$ m is placed so that its centre is at the point identified on the diagonal. Find the maximum and minimum distances between the surface of the sphere and the faces of the parallelepiped. If the sphere is allowed to slide with its centre on the diagonal, find the position of the centre of the sphere at rest.

Use ruler and compass to draw three circles, each of radius $3$ cm, so that each circle touches the others. Now draw the circle in the open space surrounded by the three circles so that it touches each of the three circles. Find the total area of the three spaces surrounded by the four circles drawn.
Find the solution set of the following equation and inequality: (a) $x^2-3x+4=x(x-1)-2(x-2)$; (b) $\dfrac{x^2-1}{x}\le 0$.
Find the solution, if any, of the following equations: (a) $2x-1+3(x+1)=5(x-1)$; (b) $\sqrt{x^2+1}=x-1$; (c) $|x-1|+|x|=2$.

A plane is moving horizontally with a speed of $200$ km/h. There is a ground station on the vertical plane through the horizontal line along which the plane is moving. When the plane reaches a definite location, the inclination of the ground station with the horizontal line is found to be $15^\circ$. After one minute that inclination is found to be $20^\circ$. After how much time will the inclination be $30^\circ$? When will the plane come just above the ground station? At what height is the plane moving?
Solve the equation $$\log_6(x+1)+\log_6(x-4)=1.$$
If $k$ is an even number, then for what values of $x$ and $y$ do we have $$x^{2k}-(xy)^k+y^{2k}=0?$$

$OAB$ is a quadrant of radius $7$ cm. Two more half circles are drawn using $OA$ and $OB$ as diameters. Find the total area of the shaded part. (For ease of calculation use $\pi=22/7$.)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bds_2005_p5_fig.png
Using a geometric progression, express $0.888\ldots$ (that is, $0.\overline{8}$) as a proper fraction.
How many minutes after 12:00 will the hour and minute hands make a $90^\circ$ angle?
Find the coordinates of the vertex of the curve $y=x^2+2x+3$.

(a) The equation $x^3-8=0$ has three roots; we know one of them, which is $x=2$; the other two are complex. A number is called complex if it contains $\sqrt{-1}=i$. The other two roots of the equation have the form $-1+ia$ and $-1-ia$. Find $a$. (Remember $i^2=-1$.) (b) Check if your results are correct.

A flat piece of cardboard measuring $10$ cm by $8$ cm has a square of side $x$ cut from each corner, and the sides are folded up to make an open box with a base of area $24\text{ cm}^2$. Find $x$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bds_2005_p11_fig.png
(a) What is the greatest number of points of intersection of ten lines? (b) What is the greatest number of points of intersection of $n$ lines?
Solve the equation $$4^x-3^{x-\frac12}=3^{x+\frac12}-2^{2x-1}.$$

The 1st, 2nd and 3rd terms of an arithmetic series are $a$, $b$ and $a^2$, where $a$ is negative. The 1st, 2nd and 3rd terms of a geometric series are $a$, $a^2$ and $b$. Find (a) the values of $a$ and $b$; (b) the sum of the geometric series; (c) the sum of the first $40$ terms of the arithmetic series.
Prove that $2^p-1$ is not a prime number if $p$ is not a prime number.
Find the last two (rightmost) digits of $3^{999}$.
Find the difference of the areas of the external and internal squares of a circle of radius $5$ cm.
$AB$ and $CD$ are diameters of the circle with center $O$. Also $AB$ is perpendicular to $CD$, and chord $DF$ intersects $AB$ at $E$. If $DE=6$ and $EF=2$, what is the area of the circle?
Solve the equation $$\sqrt{3-x}+1=x.$$
Find the value of $\cos\frac{\pi}{8}$ using the well-known identity $\cos\frac{\vartheta}{2}=\pm\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos\vartheta}{2}}$.
Two circles with centres $O$ and $O'$ touch each other externally at $A$. The tangent $TT'$ touches the two circles at $P$ and $Q$ respectively. Prove that $\angle PAO+\angle QAO'=90^\circ$.
If $f(x)=|x|$ and $g(x)=x^2-5$, calculate $f(f(g(f(-1))))$.
The sum and product of three successive numbers are equal; find the numbers. Find all the possible solutions.
Solve for $(x,y)$ in real numbers, where $x^x=y$ and $y^y=y$.
Writing down all the integers from $1$ to $100$ we make a large integer $$N=123456789101112\ldots9899100.$$ What will be the remainder if we divide $N$ by $3$?

A square has sides of length $2$. Let $S$ be the set of all line segments that have length $2$ and whose endpoints are on adjacent sides of the square. Let $L$ be the set of the midpoints of all segments in $S$. Find the area enclosed by $L$.
Two parallel chords of a circle have lengths $10$ and $14$. The distance between them is $6$. The chord parallel to these chords and halfway between them has length $\sqrt{a}$. Find $a$.

A ball is thrown vertically upward to a height of $625$ meters from the ground. Each time it hits the ground, it bounces to $2/5$ of the height it fell in the previous stage. How far will the ball travel before it stops?
What is the area of the region bounded by $$|x+y|+|x-y|=4,$$ where $x,y$ are real numbers?
Find the smallest positive integer $n>1$ such that $\sqrt{1+2+3+\cdots+n}$ is an integer. Note: $n<10$.
Let $m+12=p^a$ and $m-12=p^b$, where $a,b,m$ are integers and $p$ is a prime number. Find all possible primes $p>0$. [Note: $p$ only takes three values.]
If $x^2+3x-4$ is a factor of $x^3+bx^2+cx+11$, then find the values of $b$ and $c$.

A drawer in a room contains $100$ black socks, $80$ blue socks, $60$ red socks and $40$ purple socks. Someone randomly selects one sock at a time from the drawer, but is unable to see the color of the sock until he has taken it out of the drawer. What is the smallest number of socks that must be taken out to guarantee that $10$ pairs have been taken out? [A pair of socks $=2$ socks of the same color.]
Find the area of the largest square inscribed in a triangle of sides $5$, $6$ and $7$.
Find the remainder on dividing $(x^{100}-2x^{51}+1)$ by $(x^2-1)$.
Prove that if $a$ and $b$ are two integers, then $a\cdot b=\operatorname{LCM}(a,b)\cdot\operatorname{GCD}(a,b)$.
The sum of the first $2008$ odd positive integers is subtracted from the sum of the first $2008$ even positive integers. Find the result.

One coin is labeled with the number $1$, two different coins are labeled with the number $2$, three different coins are labeled with the number $3$, $\ldots$, $49$ different coins are labeled with the number $49$, and fifty different coins are labeled with the number $50$. All of these coins are then put into a black bag. The coins are then randomly drawn one by one. We need $10$ coins of any type. What is the minimum number of coins that must be drawn to make sure that we have at least $10$ coins of one type?
Let $a$ be an integer. The number $m$ which has the form $m=4a+3$ is a multiple of $11$. If we divide $a^4$ by $11$, what is the remainder? Show with proof.
The function $f(x)$ is a complicated nonlinear function. It satisfies $f(x)+f(1-x)=1$. Evaluate $\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx$.

Asmaa and her brother Ahmed are chess players. Asmaa's son Shamim and her daughter Sharmeen are also chess players. The worst player's twin (who is one of the $4$ chess players) and the best player are of the opposite sex. The worst player and the best player are the same age. Who is the worst player?

The three numbers $1,2,3$ are used to make a $5$-digit number. The five-digit number must contain at least one $1$, at least one $2$, and at least one $3$. How many such five-digit numbers can be made? (Hint: First count the number of words missing either a $1$ or a $2$ or a $3$.)
Find all integer solutions $(m,n)$ of $1+5\cdot2^m=n^2$.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $AB=BC=CD$ and $AC\ne BD$. Let $E$ be the intersection point of the diagonals of $ABCD$. We have $AE=DE$ if and only if $\angle BAD+\angle ADC=\vartheta$. Find $\vartheta$.

A quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $\angle BAD+\angle ADC>180^\circ$ circumscribes a circle of center $I$. A line through $I$ meets $AB$ and $CD$ at points $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Prove that if $IX=IY$, then $AX\cdot DY=BX\cdot CY$.
$300$ politicians are sitting in a room. Each one is corrupt or honest. At least one is honest. Given any two politicians, at least one is corrupt. How many are corrupt and how many are honest?
Find all integral solutions of the equation $$\frac{x^2}{2}+\frac{5}{y}=7.$$

Triangle $ABC$ is acute with the property that the bisector of $\angle BAC$, the altitude from $B$ to side $AC$ and the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ intersect at one point. Determine the angle $\angle BAC$.

Triangle $ABC$ is acute and $M$ is its circumcenter. Determine which points $P$ inside the triangle satisfy $$1\le\frac{\angle APB}{\angle ACB}\le2,\qquad 1\le\frac{\angle BPC}{\angle BAC}\le2,\qquad 1\le\frac{\angle CPA}{\angle CBA}\le2.$$

In triangle $ABC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$. $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Choose $D$ on $AC$ such that $AD=AM$. The circumcircles of triangles $AMC$ and $BDC$ intersect at $C$ and at a point $P$. What is the ratio of angles $$\frac{\angle ACB}{\angle PCB}?$$

Forty MOVers (Mathematical Olympiad Volunteers) are sitting in a circle. Munir Hasan randomly chooses $3$ volunteers to help in the awards ceremony. In how many ways can the volunteers be chosen such that at least $2$ of the volunteers were sitting next to each other before being chosen?

How many positive prime numbers can be written as an alternating sequence of $1$'s and $0$'s where the first and last digits are $1$? An alternating sequence of $1$'s and $0$'s is, for example, $N=1010101$, and it has the property that $99N=99999999$.

The region $A$ is bounded by the $x$-axis, the line $y=\frac{x}{2}$, and the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{9}+y^2=1$. The region $B$ is bounded by the $y$-axis, the line $y=mx$, and the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{9}+y^2=1$. Find $m$ such that the area of region $A$ is equal to the area of region $B$.

Each square of an $n\times n$ chessboard is either red or green. The board is colored such that in any $2\times2$ block of adjacent squares there are exactly $2$ green squares and $2$ red squares. How many ways can the chessboard be colored in this way? Note that the number of ways for a $2\times2$ chessboard is $6$ and the number of ways for a $3\times3$ chessboard is $14$, which is bigger than $2^3$.

$H$ is the orthocenter of acute triangle $ABC$. The triangle is inscribed in a circle with center $K$ and radius $R=1$. Let $D$ be the intersection of the lines $HK$ and $BC$. Also, $DK\cdot(DK-DH)=1$. Find the area of the region $ABHC$.
There are $20$ people at a party excluding you. It is known that you know the same number of people as you don't know. How many of them do you know?

Isosceles triangle $ABC$ is right-angled at $B$ and $AB=3$. A circle of unit radius is drawn with its centre on any of the vertices of this triangle. Find the maximum value of the area of that part of the triangle that is not shared by the circle.
Solve for real $x$: $$\frac{x^2-1}{x-2}=x.$$

A series is formed in the following manner: $A(1)=1$; $A(n)$ = $f(m)$ digits $f(m)$ followed by $f(m)$ digits $0$, where $m$ is the number of digits in $A(n-1)$ and $f(m)$ is the remainder when $m$ is divided by $9$. Find $A(30)$.

Triangle $ABC$ is right-angled at $B$. The bisector of $\angle BAC$ meets $BC$ at $D$. Let $G$ denote the centroid (common point of the medians) of triangle $ABC$. Suppose that $GD$ is parallel to $AB$. Find $\angle C$.
Find, with proof, all the perfect squares each of which is the product of four consecutive odd natural numbers.
Replace each asterisk in the seven-digit number $13{*}{*}45{*}$ by different digits such that the resulting number is divisible by $792$. Give a proof.

Triangle $ABC$ is right-angled at $A$. Let $D$ be a point on $BC$. $E$ and $F$ are the reflections of $D$ in $AC$ and $AB$ respectively. Prove that $[ABC]\ge[DEF]$. Find all possible positions of $D$ for equality. (Here $[X]$ denotes the area of $X$.)
Find all prime numbers $p$ and positive integers $a$ and $b$ such that $p^a+p^b$ is the square of an integer.
In a set of $131$ natural numbers, no number has a prime factor greater than $42$. Prove that it is possible to choose four numbers from this set such that their product is a perfect square.

There are $2011$ mathematicians at a party. It is known that Mahbub, the host of the party (who is also a mathematician), knows all the other mathematicians. Two mutually unacquainted mathematicians will become friends eventually after the party if they have a common friend/acquaintance (who will introduce them to each other, of course). After the end of the party, how many pairs of mathematicians will be left who are not yet introduced to each other?

In the first round of a chess tournament, each player plays against every other player exactly once. A player gets $3$, $0$ or $-1$ points respectively for winning, drawing or losing a match. After the end of the first round, is it possible that the sum of the scores of all the players is $21$? State your answer with reasoning.
In triangle $ABC$, the incircle touches $AB$, $BC$ and $CA$ at $D$, $E$ and $F$. Show that if $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEF$ are similar, then $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral.

$E$ is the midpoint of side $BC$ of rectangle $ABCD$. A point $X$ is chosen on $BE$. $DX$ meets the extension of $AB$ at $P$. Find, with proof, the position of $X$ for which the sum of the areas of $\triangle BPX$ and $\triangle DXC$ is maximum.

$ABC$ is a scalene triangle with $\angle A=90^\circ$. The tangent line at $A$ to its circumcircle meets line $BC$ at $M$, and the incircle touches $AC$ at $S$ and $AB$ at $R$. The lines $RS$ and $BC$ intersect at $N$, while the lines $AM$ and $SR$ intersect at $U$. Prove that triangle $UMN$ is isosceles.
$p$ is a prime and the sum of the numbers from $1$ to $p$ is divisible by all primes less than or equal to $p$. Find the value of $p$ with proof.

Consider a group of $n>1$ people. Any two people of this group are related by mutual friendship or mutual enmity. Any friend of a friend and any enemy of an enemy is a friend. If $A$ and $B$ are friends/enemies, then we count it as $1$ friendship/enmity. It is observed that the number of friendships and the number of enmities are equal in the group. Find all possible values of $n$.

Bhaskaracharya has set up a strange study group. Any member of that group has exactly one immediate teacher (the teacher who teaches him) except for Bhaskaracharya himself, although a teacher of a teacher is also respected as a teacher. As the chancellor of the group, Bhaskaracharya is not taught by anybody. No two members of that group can be teachers of each other. The study group operates in pairs, where each pair consists of one member and his immediate teacher. If such a pairing is possible, is it unique? Justify your answer.
Prove that $$\sqrt[100]{\sqrt3+\sqrt2}+\sqrt[100]{\sqrt3-\sqrt2}$$ is irrational.
The repeat of a natural number is obtained by writing it twice in a row (for example, the repeat of $123$ is $123123$). Find a positive integer (if any) whose repeat is a perfect square.

Subrata writes a letter to Ruponti every day (in successive intervals of $24$ hours) from Korea. But Ruponti receives the letters in intervals of $25$ hours. What is the number of the letter Ruponti receives on the $25$th day?

When Tanvir climbed the Tajingdong mountain, on his way to the top he saw it raining $11$ times. At Tajingdong, on a rainy day, it rains either in the morning or in the afternoon, but it never rains twice in the same day. On his way, Tanvir spent $16$ mornings and $13$ afternoons without rain. How many days did it take Tanvir to climb the Tajingdong mountain in total?
In a given pentagon $ABCDE$, triangles $ABC$, $BCD$, $CDE$, $DEA$ and $EAB$ all have the same area. The lines $AC$ and $AD$ intersect $BE$ at points $M$ and $N$. Prove that $BM=EN$.

Find the total number of triangles all of whose sides are integers and whose longest side has length $10$. If the same condition is applied to isosceles triangles, what will be the total number of triangles?

In triangle $ABC$, medians $AD$ and $CF$ intersect at point $G$. $P$ is an arbitrary point on $AC$. $PQ$ and $PR$ are parallel to $AD$ and $CF$ respectively. $PQ$ intersects $BC$ at $Q$ and $PR$ intersects $AB$ at $R$. If $QR$ intersects $AD$ at $M$ and $CF$ at $N$, then prove that the area of triangle $GMN$ is $S/8$, where $S$ is the area enclosed by $PQ$, $PR$, $AD$, $CF$.
Show that for any prime $p$, there are either infinitely many or no positive integers $a$ such that $6p$ divides $a^p+1$. Find all those primes for which there exists no solution.

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, $\angle A=60^\circ$. Prove that the bisector of one of the angles formed by the altitudes drawn from $B$ and $C$ passes through the center of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

The vertices of a right triangle $ABC$ inscribed in a circle divide the circumference into three arcs. The right angle is at $A$, so that the opposite arc $BC$ is a semicircle while arc $AB$ and arc $AC$ are supplementary. To each of the three arcs, we draw a tangent such that its point of tangency is the midpoint of that portion of the tangent intercepted by the extended lines $AB$ and $AC$. More precisely, the point $D$ on arc $BC$ is the midpoint of the segment joining the points $D'$ and $D''$ where the tangent at $D$ intersects the extended lines $AB$ and $AC$. Similarly for $E$ on arc $AC$ and $F$ on arc $AB$. Prove that triangle $DEF$ is equilateral.
Consider an $n\times n$ grid of points. Prove that no matter how we choose $2n-1$ points from these, there will always be a right triangle with vertices among these $2n-1$ points.
A triomino is an L-shaped pattern made from three unit squares. A $2^k\times2^k$ chessboard has one of its squares missing. Show that the remaining board can be covered with triominoes.
If $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a function such that $f(x)=-f(-x)=f(x+1)$ for all real $x$, then what is the value of $f(2013)$?

A polygon is called degenerate if one of its vertices falls on the line that joins its two neighboring vertices. In a pentagon $ABCDE$, $AB=AE$, $BC=DE$. $P$ and $Q$ are the midpoints of $AE$ and $AB$. $PQ\parallel CD$, and $BD$ is perpendicular to both $AB$ and $DE$. Prove that $ABCDE$ is a degenerate pentagon.

Let $ABCDEF$ be a regular hexagon with $AB=7$. $M$ is the midpoint of $DE$. $AC$ and $BF$ intersect at $P$, $AC$ and $BM$ intersect at $Q$, $AM$ and $BF$ intersect at $R$. Find the value of $[APB]+[BQC]+[ARF]-[PQMR]$. Here $[X]$ denotes the area of polygon $X$.
$ABCD$ is a quadrilateral where $\angle B=\angle D=90^\circ$. $E$ and $F$ are two points on $BD$ such that $AE$ is perpendicular to $BD$ and $CF\parallel AE$. Prove that $DE=BF$.

$ABCD$ is a paddy field of trapezoidal shape. Growth of paddy has been uniform everywhere in the field. Farmers are cutting the paddy and piling it at the nearest edge ($AB$, $BC$, $CD$ or $DA$). What portion of the total paddy is piled up at the side $CD$? It is given that $\angle DAB=\angle ABC=120^\circ$, $\angle BCD=\angle CDA=60^\circ$, $AB=BC=50$ units.

There are some boys and girls in a class. Every boy knows exactly $r$ girls, and every girl knows exactly $r$ boys. Show that there are equal numbers of boys and girls in the class. (Assume that knowing is mutual, i.e. if $A$ knows $B$ then $B$ knows $A$.)

There are $n$ cities in a country. Between any two cities there is at most one road. Suppose that the total number of roads is $n$. Prove that there is a city such that, starting from there, it is possible to come back to it without ever travelling the same road twice.

If there exists a prime number $p$ such that $p+2q$ is prime for all positive integers $q$ smaller than $p$, then $p$ is called an awesome prime. Find the largest awesome prime and prove that it is indeed the largest such prime.

Six points $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$, $F$ are chosen on a circle anticlockwise. None of $AB$, $CD$, $EF$ is a diameter. Extended $AB$ and $DC$ meet at $Z$, $CD$ and $FE$ at $X$, $EF$ and $BA$ at $Y$. $AC$ and $BF$ meet at $P$, $CE$ and $BD$ at $Q$, and $AE$ and $DF$ at $R$. If $O$ is the point of intersection of $YQ$ and $ZR$, find the angle $\angle XOP$.
If $x$ is divided by $10$, then the quotient is $y$ and the remainder is $3$. If $x$ and $y$ are both positive integers, then what will be the remainder if $x$ is divided by $5$?

Subrata has invented a new type of clock, according to which there are $15$ hours in each day and $80$ minutes in each hour. For example, Subrata's clock shows 10:00 when the actual time is 16:00. If the time is 18:42 on a traditional clock, then what will be the time on Subrata's clock?

Closing his eyes, Towsif begins to place knights on a chessboard of $19\times21$. After placing how many knights will Towsif be sure that on the next move at least one knight will attack another one? (In one move a knight goes straight for $2$ steps and the $3$rd step should be at a right angle to the previous path.)

In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=90^\circ$. A circle is drawn taking $AB$ as a chord. $O$ is the center of the circle. $O$ and $C$ are not on the same side of $AB$. $BD$ is perpendicular to $AC$. Prove that $BD$ is a tangent to the circle if and only if $\angle BAO=\angle BAC$.

$97+98+\cdots+114+115=2014$. Here the sum of $19$ consecutive numbers is $2014$. Find the largest number of consecutive positive integers whose sum is exactly $2014$, and justify why this must be the largest number.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle with $\angle C=60^\circ$. Perpendiculars $AA_1$ and $BB_1$ are drawn from points $A$ and $B$ to the sides $BC$ and $AC$ respectively. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$. What is the value of $\dfrac{\angle A_1MB_1}{\angle A_1CB_1}$?

If the lengths of two altitudes drawn from two vertices of a triangle to their opposite sides are $2014$ and $1$ unit, then what will be the length of the altitude drawn from the third vertex of the triangle to its opposite side?

There are $n$ players in a chess tournament. Every player plays every other player exactly once, and there are no draws. Prove that the players can be labeled $1,2,\ldots,n$ so that $i$ beats $i+1$ for each $i\in\{1,2,3,\ldots,n-1\}$.

Suppose that you are at the leftmost bottom point of an $n\times n$ grid. You have to reach the rightmost topmost point. But the rule is that you can move only in the upward or rightward direction; you cannot move down or to the left. And as there are mines at the points which are along the diagonal, you cannot go to those places either. Determine how many ways there are to reach the destination.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bds_2014_p10_fig.png

A crime is committed during the hartal. There are four witnesses. The witnesses are logicians and make the following statements: Witness One says exactly one of the four witnesses is a liar. Witness Two says exactly two of the four witnesses are liars. Witness Three says exactly three of the four witnesses are liars. Witness Four says exactly four of the four witnesses are liars. Assume that each of these statements is either true or false. How many of the witnesses are liars?
How many pairs of integers $(m,n)$ satisfy the equation $m+n=mn$?

Given a positive integer $n$, let $p(n)$ be the product of the non-zero digits of $n$. If $n$ has only one digit, then $p(n)=n$. Let $S=p(1)+p(2)+\cdots+p(999)$. What is the largest prime factor of $S$?

There were $36$ participants at a BdMO event. Some of the participants shook hands with each other, but no two participants shook hands with each other more than once. Each participant recorded the number of handshakes they made. It was found that no two participants with the same number of handshakes had shaken hands with each other. Find the maximum number of handshakes at the party. (When two participants shake hands with each other, this is counted as one handshake.)

A tetrahedron is a polyhedron composed of four triangular faces. Faces $ABC$ and $BCD$ of tetrahedron $ABCD$ meet at an angle of $\pi/6$. The area of triangle $\triangle ABC$ is $120$. The area of triangle $\triangle BCD$ is $80$, and $BC=10$. What is the volume of the tetrahedron? We call the volume of a tetrahedron one-third of the area of its base times its height.

Trapezoid $ABCD$ has sides $AB=92$, $BC=50$, $CD=19$, $AD=70$. The side $AB$ is parallel to $CD$. A circle with center $P$ on $AB$ is drawn tangent to $BC$ and $AD$. Given that $AP=m/n$, where $m,n$ are integers that have no common factors (they are relatively prime), what is $m+n$?

In triangle $\triangle ABC$, the points $A'$, $B'$, $C'$ are on sides $BC$, $AC$, $AB$ respectively. Also, $AA'$, $BB'$, $CC'$ intersect at the point $O$ (they are concurrent at $O$). Also, $$\frac{AO}{OA'}+\frac{BO}{OB'}+\frac{CO}{OC'}=92.$$ Find the value of $$\frac{AO}{OA'}\cdot\frac{BO}{OB'}\cdot\frac{CO}{OC'}.$$
(a) How many positive integer factors does $6000$ have? (b) How many positive integer factors of $6000$ are not perfect squares?
$\triangle ABC$ is isosceles with $AB=AC$. $P$ is a point inside $\triangle ABC$ such that $\angle BCP=30^\circ$, $\angle APB=150^\circ$ and $\angle CAP=39^\circ$. Find $\angle BAP$.

Consider the set of integers $\{1,2,\ldots,100\}$. Let $\{x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{100}\}$ be some arbitrary arrangement of the integers $\{1,2,\ldots,100\}$, where all of the $x_i$ are different. Find the smallest possible value of the sum $$S=|x_2-x_1|+|x_3-x_2|+\cdots+|x_{100}-x_{99}|+|x_1-x_{100}|.$$

Suppose there are $m$ Martians and $n$ Earthlings at an intergalactic peace conference. To ensure the Martians stay peaceful at the conference, we must make sure that no two Martians sit together, so that between any two Martians there is always at least one Earthling. (a) Suppose all $m+n$ Martians and Earthlings are seated in a line. How many ways can the Earthlings and Martians be seated in a line? (b) Suppose now that the $m+n$ Martians and Earthlings are seated around a circular round table. How many ways can the Earthlings and Martians be seated around the round table?

$\triangle ABC$ is an isosceles triangle with $AC=BC$ and $\angle ACB<60^\circ$. $I$ and $O$ are the incenter and circumcenter of $\triangle ABC$. The circumcircle of $\triangle BIO$ intersects $BC$ at $D\ne B$. (a) Do the lines $AC$ and $DI$ intersect? Give a proof. (b) What is the angle of intersection between the lines $OD$ and $IB$?

Aasma is a mathematician and devised an algorithm to find a husband. The strategy is: (1) Start interviewing a maximum of $1000$ prospective husbands. Assign a ranking $r$ to each person that is a positive integer. No two prospects will have the same rank $r$. (2) Reject the first $k$ men and let $H$ be the highest rank of these $k$ men. (3) After rejecting the first $k$ men, select the next prospect with a rank greater than $H$ and then stop the search immediately. If no candidate is selected after $999$ interviews, the $1000$th person is selected. Aasma wants to find the value of $k$ for which she has the highest probability of choosing the highest-ranking prospect among all $1000$ candidates without having to interview all $1000$ prospects.

(a) What is the probability that the highest-ranking prospect among all $1000$ prospects is the $(m+1)$th prospect?
(b) Assume the highest-ranking prospect is the $(m+1)$th person to be interviewed. What is the probability that the highest-ranked candidate among the first $m$ candidates is one of the first $k$ candidates who were rejected?
(c) What is the probability that the prospect with the highest rank is the $(m+1)$th person and that Aasma will choose the $(m+1)$th person using this algorithm?
(d) The total probability that Aasma will choose the highest-ranking prospect among the $1000$ prospects is the sum of the probabilities for each possible value of $m+1$, with $m+1$ ranging between $k+1$ and $1000$. Find the sum. To simplify your answer use the formula $$\log N\approx\frac{1}{N-1}+\frac{1}{N-2}+\cdots+\frac12+\frac11.$$
(e) Find the value of $k$ that maximizes the probability of choosing the highest-ranking prospect without interviewing all $1000$ candidates. You may need to know that the maximum of the function $x\log\frac{A}{x-1}$ is approximately $(A+1)/e$, where $A$ is a constant and $e$ is Euler's number, $e=2.718\ldots$

$\triangle ABC$ is inscribed in circle $\omega$ with $AB=5$, $BC=7$, $AC=3$. The bisector of $\angle A$ meets side $BC$ at $D$ and circle $\omega$ at a second point $E$. Let $\gamma$ be the circle with diameter $DE$. Circles $\omega$ and $\gamma$ meet at $E$ and at a second point $F$. Then $AF^2=m/n$, where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers. Find $m+n$.

Bangladesh plays India in a best-of-5 game series. The team that wins $3$ games first wins the series. The series can end after $3$ games, $4$ games or $5$ games. If Bangladesh and India are equally strong, calculate (a) the probability that Bangladesh wins the series in $3$ games; (b) the probability that Bangladesh wins the series in $4$ games; (c) the probability that the series ends in exactly $5$ games.

$\triangle ABC$ is an isosceles triangle with $AB=AC$, inscribed in a circle with center $O$ and diameter $AD$. The diameter intersects $BC$ at $E$, and $F$ is the midpoint of $OE$. Given that $BD\parallel FC$ and $BC=25$, find the length of $CD$.
The roots of the equation $x^2+3x-1=0$ are also roots of the quartic equation $x^4+ax^2+bx+c=0$. Find the value of $a+b+4c$.

The circular arcs $AC$ and $BC$ have centers at $B$ and $A$ respectively. There exists a circle tangent to both arcs $AC$ and $BC$ and to the line segment $AB$. The length of the arc $BC$ is $12$. What is the circumference of the circle?

$8$ congruent equilateral triangles, each of a different colour, are used to construct a regular octahedron. How many distinguishable ways are there to construct the octahedron? (Two coloured octahedra are distinguishable if neither can be rotated to look just like the other.)

$100$ pictures of BdMO math campers were painted by Urmi. Exactly $k$ colors were used in each picture. There is a common color in every $20$ pictures, but there is no color common to all $100$ pictures. Find the smallest possible value of $k$.

The sequence $\{a_n\}$ is defined by $a_0=1$, $a_1=1$ and $a_{n+1}=2(a_n-a_{n-1})$ for all positive integers $n$. What is the remainder of $a_{2016}$ upon division by $2017$? Provide a proof of your answer.

In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ with circumcenter $O$, the lines $BC$ and $AD$ intersect at $E$. The lines $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at $F$. A point $P$ satisfying $\angle EPD=\angle FPD=\angle BAD$ is chosen inside $ABCD$. The line $FO$ intersects the lines $AD$, $EP$, $BC$ at $X$, $Q$, $Y$ respectively. Also $\angle DQX=\angle CQY$. What is $\angle AEB$?

$p$ is an odd prime. The integer $k$ is in the range $1\le k\le p-1$. Let $a_k$ be the number of divisors of $kp+1$ that are greater than or equal to $k$ and less than $p$. Find the value of $a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_{p-1}$.
Find the real solutions of the equation $$x^2(2-x)^2=1+2(1-x)^2.$$
$AB$ is a diameter of a circle. Tangents $AD$ and $BC$ are drawn so that $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at a point on the circle. Suppose $AD=a$ and $BC=b$, with $a\ne b$. What is the diameter $AB$?

Urmi rolls four fair six-sided dice. She doesn't see the results. Her friend Ipshita tells her that the product of the numbers is $144$. Ipshita also says that the sum of the dice, $S$, satisfies $14\le S\le18$. Urmi tells Ipshita that $S$ cannot be one of the numbers in the set $\{14,15,16,17,18\}$ if the product is $144$. Which number in the set $\{14,15,16,17,18\}$ is an impossible value for $S$?
Sabbir is counting the minimum number $m$ of lines that can be drawn in the plane so that they intersect in exactly $200$ distinct points. What is $m$?

Four circles are drawn with the sides of quadrilateral $ABCD$ as diameters. The two circles passing through $A$ meet again at $A'$. The two circles passing through $B$ meet again at $B'$. The two circles passing through $C$ meet again at $C'$. The two circles passing through $D$ meet again at $D'$. Suppose $A'$, $B'$, $C'$, $D'$ are all distinct. Is the quadrilateral $A'B'C'D'$ similar to $ABCD$? Show with proof.
Find all pairs of integers $(m,n)$ satisfying the equality $$3\left(m^2+n^2\right)-7(m+n)=-4.$$
Evaluate $$\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\cos^4x+\sin x\cos^3x+\sin^2x\cos^2x+\sin^3x\cos x}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x+2\sin x\cos^3x+2\sin^2x\cos^2x+2\sin^3x\cos x}\,dx.$$

In a tournament of $n$ players, every pair of players plays exactly one match and there are no draws. A positive integer $k$ is called $n$-good if there exists a tournament of $n$ players in which, for any $k$ players, there is at least one player other than these $k$ players who beats all of them. (i) Prove that if $k$ is $n$-good then $n\ge2^{k+1}-1$. (ii) Find all $n$ such that $2$ is $n$-good.

At some math olympiad, $72$ medals were handed out. Afterwards, it was found that Sumon had lost the receipt! He only remembers that the total price of the medals was a $5$-digit number, and the three middle digits were all $9$. If the price of every medal was the same integer, what was the amount spent on each medal?
Prove that if $a,b,c$ are positive real numbers, then $$\frac{a}{bc}+\frac{b}{ca}+\frac{c}{ab}\ge\frac2a+\frac2b-\frac2c.$$
Find all prime numbers such that the square of the prime number can be written as the sum of the cubes of two positive integers.

In this figure $ABCD$ is a trapezium with $AB\parallel CD$. $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ are the midpoints of $AB$, $BD$, $DC$, $CA$ respectively. $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. The area of $\triangle AOB$ is $2019$ and the area of $\triangle COD$ is $2020$. What is the area of quadrilateral $PQRS$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bds_2019_p4_fig.png

Let $\alpha$ and $\omega$ be two circles such that $\omega$ goes through the center of $\alpha$. $\omega$ intersects $\alpha$ at $A$ and $B$. Let $P$ be any point on the circumference of $\omega$. The lines $PA$ and $PB$ intersect $\alpha$ again at $E$ and $F$ respectively. Prove that $AB=EF$.

Consider a $9\times9$ array of white squares. Find the largest $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with the property: no matter how one chooses $n$ of the $81$ white squares and colors them black, there always remains a $1\times4$ array of white squares (either vertical or horizontal).
$M$ and $N$ are two positive integers with $M\ne N$, and $(M,N)=M^2-N^2+MN$. Show that $MN$ is a perfect cube.

Prove that for all positive integers $n$ we can find a permutation of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ such that the average of any two numbers does not appear in between them. For example, $\{1,3,2,4\}$ works, but $\{1,2,3,4\}$ does not, because $2$ is between $1$ and $3$.

Given three concentric circles $\omega_1$, $\omega_2$, $\omega_3$ with radii $r_1$, $r_2$, $r_3$ such that $r_1+r_3\ge2r_2$, construct a line that intersects $\omega_3$, $\omega_2$, $\omega_1$ at $A$, $B$, $C$ respectively such that $AB=BC$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bds_2019_p9_fig.png

In chess, a normal knight goes two steps forward and one step to the side, in some orientation. Thanic thought that he should spice the game up a bit, so he introduced a new kind of piece called a warrior. A warrior can either go three steps forward and one step to the side, or two steps forward and two steps to the side, in some orientation. On a $2020\times2020$ chessboard, prove that the maximum number of warriors such that none of them attack each other is less than or equal to $2/5$ of the number of cells.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bds_2019_p10_fig.png
Let $m$ be a real number such that the following equation holds: $$3^m=4m.$$ Compute the sum of all possible distinct values that $\dfrac{3^{(3^m)}}{m^4}$ can take.

A polygon is called beautiful if you can pick three of its vertices to have an angle of $144$ degrees between them. Compute the number of integers $n$ greater than $8$ and not greater than $2024$ for which a regular $n$-gon is beautiful.

In a party of $11$ people, certain pairs of people shake hands with each other. In every group of three people, there exists one person who shakes hands with the other two. What is the minimum number of handshakes that can take place in this party?

$ABCD$ is a square. $P$ and $Q$ are two points on segments $BC$ and $CD$ respectively such that $\angle APQ=90^\circ$. It is given that $AP=4$ and $PQ=1$. If we express the length of segment $AB$ as $m/n$ in lowest terms, compute $m+10n$.
Let $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ be real numbers such that for all $n>0$, $x_{n+3}=x_{n+2}-2x_{n+1}+x_n$. Suppose $x_1=x_3=1$ and you are given that $x_{98}=x_{99}$. Find the sum $x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_{100}$.

A permutation $(a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots,a_n)$ of the numbers $(1,2,3,\ldots,n)$ is called almost-sorted if there exists exactly one $i\in\{1,2,3,\ldots,n-1\}$ such that $a_i>a_{i+1}$. What is the number of almost-sorted permutations of the numbers $(1,2,3,\ldots,13)$?

Let $f$ be a function from the set of positive integers to the set of positive integers such that for each positive integer $n$, if $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_s$ are all the positive divisors of $n$, then $f(x_1)f(x_2)\cdots f(x_s)=n$. Find the sum of all possible values of $f(343)+f(3012)$.
Let $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be such that $$f(f(x+y))=f(x^2)+f(y^2)\quad\text{and}\quad f(f(2020))=1010.$$ Find $f(2025)$.

In triangle $ABC$, $AB=12$, $BC=20$, $CA=16$. $X$ and $Y$ are two points on segments $AB$ and $AC$ respectively. $K$ is a point on segment $XY$ such that $XK/KY=7/5$. If we let $X$ and $Y$ vary on segments $AB$ and $AC$, all the positions of $K$ cover a region. If we express the area of that region as $m/n$ in lowest terms, compute $m+n$.

Rahul is at $(3,3)$ on the coordinate plane. In each step he can move one unit up or one unit to the right. He loves primes, and will never visit a coordinate point where both coordinates are composite. In how many ways can he reach $(20,13)$?

Urmi is playing a game on a computer. If the computer screen displays the number $x$, then in the next move Urmi can do one of the following: (i) replace $x$ by $4x+1$; (ii) replace $x$ by the largest integer not greater than $x/2$. Initially the computer screen displays $0$. How many different integers less than or equal to $2020$ can Urmi achieve through a sequence of moves? It is permitted for the number displayed on the screen to exceed $2020$ during the sequence.
How many ordered pairs of integers $(m,n)$ are there such that $m$ and $n$ are the legs of a right triangle with an area equal to a prime number not exceeding $80$?
Let $x$ and $y$ be positive integers such that $2(x+y)=\gcd(x,y)+\operatorname{lcm}(x,y)$. Find $\dfrac{\operatorname{lcm}(x,y)}{\gcd(x,y)}$.

Let $r$ be a positive real number. Denote by $[r]$ the integer part of $r$ and by $\{r\}$ the fractional part of $r$. For example, if $r=32.86$, then $\{r\}=0.86$ and $[r]=32$. What is the sum of all positive numbers $r$ satisfying $25\{r\}+[r]=125$?

$ABCD$ is an isosceles trapezium such that $AD=BC$, $AB=5$ and $CD=10$. A point $E$ in the plane is such that $AE\perp EC$ and $BC=EC$. The length of $AE$ can be expressed as $a\sqrt b$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers and $b$ is not divisible by any square number other than $1$. Find the value of $(a+b)$.
$g:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is a function that satisfies $$g(x)+g(y)=g(x+y)-xy.$$ If $g(23)=0$, what is the sum of all possible values of $g(35)$?

On a table near the sea, there are $N$ glass boxes, where $N<2021$, each containing exactly $2021$ balls. Sowdha and Rafi play a game by taking turns on the boxes, where Sowdha takes the first turn. In each turn, a player selects a non-empty box and throws out some of the balls from it into the sea. If a player wants, he can throw out all of the balls in the selected box. The player who throws out the last ball wins. Let $S$ be the sum of all values of $N$ for which Sowdha has a winning strategy and let $R$ be the sum of all values of $N$ for which Rafi has a winning strategy. What is the value of $\dfrac{R-S}{10}$?

For a positive integer $n$, let $s(n)$ and $c(n)$ be the numbers of divisors of $n$ that are perfect squares and perfect cubes respectively. A positive integer $n$ is called fair if $s(n)=c(n)>1$. Find the number of fair integers less than $100$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle. The external bisector of $\angle BAC$ meets the line $BC$ at point $N$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. $P$ and $Q$ are two points on line $AN$ such that $\angle PMN=\angle MQN=90^\circ$. If $PN=5$ and $BC=3$, then the length of $QA$ can be expressed as $\frac ab$, where $a$ and $b$ are coprime positive integers. What is the value of $(a+b)$?

Cynthia loves Pokemon and she wants to catch them all. In Victory Road, there are a total of $80$ Pokemon. Cynthia wants to catch as many of them as possible. However, she cannot catch any two Pokemon that are enemies with each other. After exploring around for a while, she makes the following two observations: (1) Every Pokemon in Victory Road is enemies with exactly two other Pokemon. (2) Due to her inability to catch Pokemon that are enemies with one another, the maximum number of Pokemon she can catch is equal to $n$. What is the sum of all possible values of $n$?

A positive integer $n$ is called nice if it has at least $3$ proper divisors and it is equal to the sum of its three largest proper divisors. For example, $6$ is nice because its three largest proper divisors are $3,2,1$ and $6=3+2+1$. Find the number of nice integers not greater than $3000$.

Let $ABCD$ be a square such that $A=(0,0)$ and $B=(1,1)$. $P\left(\frac27,\frac14\right)$ is a point inside the square. An ant starts walking from $P$, touches $3$ sides of the square and comes back to the point $P$. The least possible distance travelled by the ant can be expressed as $\frac{\sqrt a}{b}$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers and $a$ is not divisible by any square number other than $1$. What is the value of $(a+b)$?

Two toads named Gamakichi and Gamatatsu are sitting at the points $(0,0)$ and $(2,0)$ respectively. Their goal is to reach $(5,5)$ and $(7,5)$ respectively by making one-unit jumps in the positive $x$ or $y$ direction at a time. How many ways can they do this while ensuring that there is no point in the plane on which both Gamakichi and Gamatatsu land?
